sections.html:
Find the Anderson County Register of Deeds at the county building, 100 North Main Street, Room 205, Clinton, TN 37716-3624. Phone 865-457-6235. Staff work the counter Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Every deed, deed of trust and similar land record in the county is filed in this room.

Looking up a record does not require a visit. The office website hosts scanned indexes and images covering January 1, 1990 forward, and viewing them costs nothing. Anderson County was the first in the country to post its indexes and images online, beginning March 24, 1997. A seller thinking of listing can view the last recorded deed, look for liens and check who owned the house earlier, all from a laptop.

The same building houses two offices you will probably need. The Assessor of Property is in Suite 202 (865-457-6225), and the Trustee, who collects county property tax, is in Room 203 (865-457-6233). Check the county's register of deeds page for current hours before you make the trip.

East Tennessee's Anderson County belongs to the Knoxville metro area. Clinton is the county seat, and Oak Ridge is the largest city. Estimated population in 2025 was 82,066, up 6.3 percent since April 2020. The county has 36,992 housing units, 71.7 percent occupied by owners, and a median owner-occupied value of $239,400 for 2020 to 2024. Many older houses around Norris and Oak Ridge go back to the dam and wartime construction years, so sellers often face deferred maintenance.

The counter staff only decide if a document can be accepted for the record. They do not judge its legal soundness, yet a deed that leaves out a required element comes back to you. Tennessee statute lists what must be there.

  • A readable original, signed, with a notary acknowledgment or comparable certificate
  • Names and addresses for the owner and the taxpayer (T.C.A. 66-24-114)
  • A reference back to the previous recorded deed, the derivation clause required by 66-24-110
  • The preparer's name and address (66-24-115)
  • The parcel identification number (66-24-122)
  • All fees, along with any transfer or mortgage tax due

A closing attorney or title company covers every item in most sales. If you are selling by yourself, call the register before you start drafting. Forgetting the parcel number is the classic error, and you find out while the buyer is standing there.

Hand-drafted deeds deserve extra care. Compare the legal description line by line with the old deed, check every name's spelling, and make sure the notary completes the acknowledgment before anyone leaves the room. Fixing a rejected deed later means another trip, another notary and possibly a delayed payout.

sections.h2: How the transfer tax works here
sections.html:
Tennessee's realty transfer tax comes from T.C.A. 67-4-409 and equals $0.37 for each $100. The register collects it as the deed is entered. By law the grantee, meaning the buyer, bears the cost. Whichever is higher, the price paid or the property's worth, sets the base.

At presentation, the buyer or the buyer's agent takes an oath on the stated value, in front of the register, and the oath appears on the face of the deed. A knowingly false figure is perjury. Later on, state revenue staff set recorded values beside the assessor's numbers. If the transfer is exempt, nobody swears to anything.

Some transfers owe nothing. A few examples: spouses creating or ending a tenancy by the entirety, an executor following a will, a divorce decree or settlement deed, and a revocable living trust receiving or returning a home for the same person or spouse. Deals with a government body are also free of the tax.

ChargeAmount
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of price or value
New-loan mortgage tax$0.115 per $100, first $2,000 exempt
Computer fee, non-UCC instruments$2.00
Each added instrument in a document$5.00
Receipt for transfer or mortgage taxUp to $1.00

The basic recording charge comes from T.C.A. 8-21-1001 and climbs with the number of pages and the kind of instrument. Ask the office at 865-457-6235 what yours will be. Non-UCC instruments pick up a $2.00 computer fee. A register whose county legislative body approves may charge $2.00 for e-filing through the county portal, though government filers skip it.

If the buyer finances, a mortgage tax is added, and the borrower covers it. Bundle a deed with a release of an old deed of trust and each extra instrument adds $5.00. Money must arrive with the papers.

Your own lender's release normally gets recorded shortly after the sale. Ask the title company who will file it and whether it costs anything.

Recording puts the buyer's name in the books, but taxes are another matter. The trustee is the collector of county property tax. Value is set as of January 1, the first Monday in October is the due date, and a bill left unpaid is delinquent on March 1 of the year after. Tax relief and the tax freeze, for the county and its cities, are also handled by the trustee.

Before the closing date, ask the trustee if this year's bill and any earlier ones are paid. The assessor, who appraises every parcel and hears owner challenges, can explain how yours was valued. Challenges go to the county board of equalization first and can then reach the State Board of Equalization.

If you are 65 or older, or disabled, find out from the trustee what relief or a freeze could do for you before you decide to sell.

sections.h2: What happens from contract to closing
sections.html:
A signed contract sends the title company or attorney off to search for liens, draft the deed and arrange the oath of value. The seller signs the deed at closing, the buyer funds the transfer tax and any mortgage tax, and the register stamps the documents with a book and page number.

Have a photo ID ready, along with the earlier deed or its recording reference, the parcel number from your tax bill and any loan payoff figures. For an inherited house, the executor's paperwork must accompany the deed.

If you would rather not repair or show the house, we buy Anderson County properties as-is. The sale still finishes with a deed recorded in this office, so the steps above apply. The difference is no lender underwriting and no mortgage tax.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Anderson County, TN?
faqs.a: Bring it to Room 205 at 100 North Main Street in Clinton, TN 37716, or call 865-457-6235 first. The counter opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 5 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Who pays the Tennessee transfer tax on a home sale?
faqs.a: Legally the buyer owes it, at $0.37 per $100 of the larger of price or value. A contract may divide closing costs another way, so read yours closely.

faqs.q: Can I search Anderson County deed records online?
faqs.a: Yes. andersondeeds.com offers free indexes and images from January 1, 1990 on. The office began online access in March 1997.

faqs.q: Does moving a house into my living trust owe transfer tax?
faqs.a: No tax is owed when you place a house in a revocable living trust that you or your spouse created, or when the trustee transfers it back. The deed still needs to meet the recording rules.

faqs.q: Is the register of deeds the same as the assessor?
faqs.a: No. The register records documents and collects transfer tax. The Assessor of Property (Suite 202, 865-457-6225) sets appraised value, and the Trustee in Room 203 collects the bill.
